requirement: The harness groups matching occurrences under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.group_hits` and renders each excerpt under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.windows`. Each entry's `node` is a reference under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference`. `complete` reports whether the search exhausted its scope.
rationale:
`requirements.sdk.graph.search.search_text.behavior` has one obligation of its own: `complete` reports whether the search exhausted its scope. The rest of the text delegates to cited requirements (`group_hits`, `windows`, `node_reference`). Those have their own tests and need no reassessment here. I still checked that the subject's tests apply them in the subject's case.

**`complete`**
- `search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot` in `project_sources.rs` runs an uncapped search and asserts `complete == true`. It then runs the same search with `limit: 1` and asserts exactly one match and `complete == false`. A truncated result that reported true would fail this.
- `scoped_text_results_keep_line_numbers_context_and_completeness` in `source_defaults.rs` covers the provider level.
  - A search with `limit(2)` over 3 hits asserts `!complete`.
  - A scoped search with `limit(2)` that returns exactly 2 hits asserts `complete`. This is the boundary where the limit is not exceeded.
  - A scoped search with `limit(1)` over 2 hits asserts `!complete`.
- `search_groups_exact_occurrences_and_records_the_selected_declaration` asserts `page["complete"] == true` on the agent-tool JSON.
- `source_reads_track_optional_dependencies_and_empty_searches_remain_discovery` asserts the delivered JSON `{"complete":true,"matches":[]}` for an empty search.
- `source_tools_forward_arguments_and_present_discovery_and_read_results` checks that `complete` is forwarded in the delivered JSON, as true and as false.
- `gitignore_is_shared_by_all_operations_with_or_without_a_git_repository` asserts `complete` for full and excluded scopes.

**Grouping (`group_hits`)**
- `search_groups_exact_occurrences_and_records_the_selected_declaration` has `const B` with two hits ("hit hit"). It asserts one entry for each enclosing item, with a single excerpt `const B: &str = "hit hit";`.
- The same test covers a multi-byte character (`é`) before a hit.
- It asserts page-local tags "1" and "2".
- It asserts that `finish_search` with `used:["2"]` records the dependency on `code.rs#const[B]`, and that `used:[]` records none.
- `search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot` asserts tag uniqueness across entries and pagination over many items.

**Windows**
- The excerpts are checked with the default window. They are clipped to the item and the hits are retained.
- Non-default `window_bytes` is not exercised in the reviewed tests. That belongs to the `windows` requirement's own tests, which the `search_groups_exact_occurrences_and_records_the_selected_declaration` test also references.

**Node reference**
- `search_groups_exact_occurrences_and_records_the_selected_declaration` asserts each entry's `node` equals the interned node of the enclosing item, serialized in the JSON page.
- The same test uses `read_node` with the match entry. It asserts the resulting dependency is on `results.matches[1].node`.

All the reviewed tests carry `{test}` references to the subject. I found no unaddressed obligation and no missing assertion.

text: The harness groups matching occurrences under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.group_hits` and renders each excerpt under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.windows`. Each entry's `node` is a reference under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference`. `complete` reports whether the search exhausted its scope.

Deliver one entry per enclosing item in a text search, even when the item has several hits. Group before pagination so an item's excerpt stays together. Each entry carries a node reference under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference`, one excerpt, and the page-local tag used by `finish_search`. The tag accounts for use of the excerpt. The node reference lets the agent read the full item.

The agent's `search_text` tool accepts a nonnegative `window_bytes`, defaulting to 128. For a hit with byte span `[start, end)`, retain the hit and up to `window_bytes` of source immediately before `start` and after `end`. Clip the window to the enclosing item's span. Move a context boundary that splits a UTF-8 character inward to the nearest character boundary. With `window_bytes: 0`, only the hit spans and the available header and trailer contribute source to the excerpt.

Compute windows for all hits in the item from the same snapshot. Where windows touch or overlap, emit the contiguous source once. This preserves each hit and the text between nearby hits, including whitespace and newlines.

The agent harness uses the unsigned integer representation of `NodeId<D>` for the current node, supplied inputs, and nodes in tool results. Built-in tools accepting a node ID resolve that integer in the domain's cache. A malformed value or an unassigned integer produces a tool error before any graph read.
For example, if a search hit contains `"node": 7`, the agent can call `read_node({"node": 7})` to read the enclosing node.
